title: Convergence
subtitle:
Avant-garde ideals, bonds forged through shared labor, and a kindred aesthetic vision.
All shared memories of the past.

trails.title: The Necessary Step
trails.description: We gather, we part—all because of a single word.

content.text:
This is a land where traditions are told through murals. After the revolution, the young government turned to its artists. This newborn Mexico had so many stories to tell, so many to shape—and paintings adorning the walls of its buildings became the perfect medium. In the 1920s, the muralist movement swept through the country.

Look, this was an art form both ancient and brand new. It no longer lived in auction houses, galleries, or the private collections of the wealthy. Instead, it unfolded across vast walls open to the public. On those walls, artists spoke of justice, of freedom, of this nation's history and memory. Imagine it! A new country, a new canvas, and so many stories to tell! From the very beginning, these murals were inseparable from politics. The brush was the artist's voice. They spoke for their ideals, for beauty, for all the suffering people of the world ...

But voices are difficult to harmonize. And they can turn harsh.

As the 20th century entered its third decade, cracks began to appear—between artist and artist, between artist and state. Should the murals depict suffering or glory? Whose praises should they sing? Which path forward? Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros—three names that once symbolized hope, our "Los Tres Grandes"—held different visions for the future of both their art and their country.

The rifts only deepened. In the small "Midnight Kitchen," young painters listened to this "fight of the century."

items.text: White smoke from burning copal fills the air, mixed with the scent of old books.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The Mexico City People's Library.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Home to the Vigiles Bureau's temporary branch.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Why here?
She lights a candle. The small flame does little to brighten the vast darkness of the room before her.
Corridor, Temporary Branch

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Wait, Añil.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I'm not sure what might lie ahead. You better stay back.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Understood. I wouldn't want to be a liability.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I'll await a certain young woman here and do my best to ensure she doesn't interfere with your actions.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Be careful, Ms. Ramona. Your safety is more important than anything.
In total silence, she walks through the familiar corridors, made unfamiliar in the dim light and strange circumstances.

She reminds herself that it is still that same place she's entered a hundred times before. The bookshelves stand in their usual order. The lobby floor shines. The only difference is that no one is here.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: They must've dispatched some top officers to the club after they got my report.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Others will be out on patrol, making sure the festival doesn't have any arcanum-related accidents.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Still, I can't believe they would just leave the place empty. That makes no sense. There must be—
Her words fade into the still air.
Around the corner, the receptionist lies passed out on the floor. Even unconscious, her face is tight with fear, as if trapped in a nightmare.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Sea? No. Help ...

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Still breathing. Trapped in a living nightmare or something.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: A whole lotta pneuma gathered here.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Someone's activated a ritual, a big one. Power of it's knocked out anyone in the area.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Who the hell'd be able to set up a large-scale arcane ritual like this in a Vigiles Bureau branch? And how?
Ramona lifts the candle and looks up toward the stairs.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: That mural, the one with the missing artist, but now it's finished.
How many times has she seen that mural? Those faces, the familiar scene, vivid yet silent, unfinished for as long as she had worked with Vigiles here.
She had never truly committed the faces of those young people in the mural to memory, but now they almost seem familiar.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Could this be the killer's final piece? And I ...
She takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I followed their marigold trail here. Am I their final target?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: You've finally come. Teresita, my dear friend!

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Teresita?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You think I'm a friend of yours? Is that why you chose me?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: You've truly forgotten everything. That's quite alright. I'll help you remember, just as you once helped me.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: This mural is my first and final piece of the era.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: A product of blood, sweat, and tears. A tribute to the Mexican mythos you held so dear, one that honors both the sacred traditions of our ancestors and our courageous struggles in the modern world.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: You see, no matter how strange this world becomes, I will never abandon our shared dream.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I incorporated each of us into the painting, just as I've done many times before. Think of it as a celebration of our rebirth.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I've waited a long time for this reunion.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Four long years, crossing several "Storms" under Manus Vindictae's protection, I chased all sorts of myths and legends, all to find a way to resurrect the dead, and I've finally found it.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: The Aztecs believed that the manner of one's death determines the soul's reincarnation.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: And so, tonight, the souls of our warriors will be reborn like butterflies emerging from their cocoons, carried on sacred winds from the north.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: This is our reunion, one not even death can keep us from.
A dripping sound breaks the quiet, but its source remains hidden.
The sense of space fades away as her mind sinks into darkness.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Sleep tight, Teresita. Fall into the dream, our irreplaceable memory of the past.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: When you awake, everything will have returned to how it was, to the beauty of our glory days.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Teresita? Who are you talking about?
Endless water stretches out before her, a lake as wide as Texcoco once had been.
A cold color guides her awareness as it moves through the Depths of Myth.
Her long journey ends when she finds her destination and slips into a fragile container made of fragments of memory.
I am ...

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: I am Teresita.
This memory container, as thin as a paper boat, floats to a stop on the water.
Around her, a rough memory forms on a stage. Happiness hangs like fog, showing how its owner once felt.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Teresita? Teresita!

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Pardon me. My mind was elsewhere. You are ...?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: My name is Muriel.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: María asked me to welcome you on her behalf. From this day forth, you're officially a fellow member of the Midnight Kitchen.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Heh. You're María's new student? Oh, sorry, I don't mean to be rude.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: I'm just surprised you're so young.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: No need to apologize. You're not the first to say so. But I've been painting for as long as I can remember.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: The Midnight Kitchen. An interesting name. An homage to Montmartre's "Laundry Ship," is it?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Hahahaha, no, nothing like that. We first started gathering in María's kitchen late at night, so Antonio suggested we name our little club after it.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: María founded it in hopes of creating a space for like-minded artists to have open and meaningful discussions. She's been planning to start a magazine on Mexico's artistic transformation.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: And she said you have some wonderful ideas and insights on the art of indigenous peoples. She said you could teach us all about it while she's away on her exhibition tour in the United States.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Well, I, I'll do my best. Though, I have to say, teaching has never been my strong suit. Don't set your expectations too high.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Besides, I'll need to look over your paintings first.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Trust me. You won't be disappointed.
The atmosphere thickens and darkens. Only uncertain, worry, and conflict remain.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Ah. You're a genius painter, Muriel. Your work will cause a stir all over the world.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: You're too kind, but as much as I appreciate such praise, you know fame has never been my goal.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: And I wouldn't accept the title of genius either. I simply love to paint, to create alongside my dear friends.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Your goals are admirable in themselves. Though more than genius, your greatest gift lies in your unending passion.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Still, I can't help but wonder if this movement is on the right track.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Hm? Is this about that article in New Masses?

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Yes. We once saw our movement as revolutionary, a force to change our society for the better, but, as Siqueiros said, it seems it may have already fallen under the thumb of the petite bourgeoisie.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: We wanted to reconceptualize our identity, history, and culture as a people. We believed that only through common understanding could we ever truly be united.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: We wanted to create a unique story. A story of Mexico.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: But have we succeeded in our goal?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Teresita ...

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: I'm having second thoughts. Painting these murals on the walls of grand buildings—perhaps it's been a mistake all along.
The world around her shifts like a maelstrom. The memory flickers in and out.
Words and feelings slash her like swirling debris caught in the storm.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Why did you turn down Lucas's invitation, Muriel?

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Paris is the center of the art world. You know Rivera went to Europe to study around your age, don't you? An opportunity like this doesn't come all that often.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I don't want to leave Mexico, Teresita. I can't.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I want to stay here, side by side with my friends.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: You saw the debate at the Palace of Fine Arts. We're at a critical turning point for the muralist movement.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Which is precisely why I want you to refine your skills in Europe, Muriel. It would do you good to free yourself from this mental turmoil.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Art can change the world. I still believe that. But there are many obstacles we need to overcome ...

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: A challenge that has kept María very busy, and for which the progress has hardly been satisfactory. *sigh* I shouldn't distract you with all this.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I'll go, if that's what you wish, Teresita.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Then do it. Make our dream come true, kiddo. The future depends on you.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Future ...

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Dream, whose dream? Mine?

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: It sounds inspiring, but ...
Her thoughts drift out of her body, caught helpless in the tide of a deep and roiling sea.
She reaches out and stirs the emotions before her. Joy and happiness fade at her touch like mist.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Why do I feel no joy at all?

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: There's nothing but sorrow here.
She whispers the words, too difficult to speak aloud.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: There's something—something long forgotten. I've got to find it.
